author: Claude
candidate_edge: A single opening-range breakout/failed-breakout signal per weekday per symbol on EURUSD and GBPUSD, gated strictly to the 07:00-08:00 UTC London cash-session open, flat by 16:00 UTC (0% overnight target). Bounded params: range window 07:00-08:00 UTC, entry = M15-confirmed close beyond range high/low (breakout) or M15-confirmed close back inside the range after a false break (failure/reversal variant, mutually exclusive per bar), stop = range width, target = 1.5x-2.0x range width, hard time-stop flat at 16:00 UTC.
confidence: Low-to-moderate. The density prior (0.6-0.7 trades/bd/symbol) is a structural inference from calendar mechanics (one opening range per weekday, discounting holidays/low-range days), not a measurement -- no existing measured configuration in the frozen Q02 screen gates entry to this specific 07:00-08:00 UTC window, so there is no direct historical R_bd for the mechanism itself. The E[R] prior (+0.10-0.15R) is anchored to the single best-measured session-flat profile in the whole inventory (13213 USDJPY Balke breakout, +0.064R, 0% overnight) scaled up for London's structurally higher realized-vol-at-open versus Tokyo's 03:00-06:00 GMT+3 window, which is itself an unverified transfer assumption and the primary thing the Q02 canary must falsify.
confounders: London-open volatility is partly driven by the same macro calendar the news-blackout filter already excludes (Hard Rule mandatory news blackout) -- if the tradeable edge is concentrated on high-impact-news days, the news filter could remove most of the density before Q02 even measures it.

EURUSD and GBPUSD daily ranges are correlated (both GBP/EUR vs USD); if the mechanism fires on both symbols from the same market-wide opening shock, the two 'independent' sleeves may share tail risk on the same days -- must be checked against the FTMO_PORTFOLIO_GAP_CURRENT.md tail-dependence method (|r|>0.30 or >2x independence-baseline lower-decile co-occurrence) before either symbol enters a book alongside the other.

Range-breakout mechanisms are regime-dependent (trend vs chop); the 2018-2024 window mixes both regimes and a single aggregate E[R] could mask a strategy that only works in a sub-period, which is exactly the failure mode the census_frontier_holdout.json finding (in-sample winners do not beat baseline OOS) already demonstrated for this EA family generally.

M15 execution timeframe means the true entry price is subject to spread widening right at the 07:00 UTC open, which the .DWX tester models as zero spread (FTMO_PORTFOLIO_GAP_CURRENT.md section 1b) -- the cost-to-target check below is therefore commission-only and may be optimistic.
observations: No measured Q02 configuration on EURUSD or GBPUSD (30 configurations in the frozen screen, see baseline_extract.json) gates entry to a fixed opening-range window; the best measured non-session-anchored config on either symbol tops out at R_bd well below the Balke 13213 template (0.048 R_bd, 0% overnight). All measured intraday sleeves that DO reach the fastest profile in the company (13213, 0.744 trades/bd) use a session-range-breakout mechanism, just on the wrong pair/session for this hypothesis (Tokyo, USDJPY) -- H-V1 asks whether the SAME mechanism class (opening-range breakout/failure), re-anchored to each symbol's OWN native cash-session open rather than transplanted verbatim (which is precisely the transplant that failed for AUDJPY/EURJPY/USDCAD/etc. in the 41484 fan-out, see baseline_extract.json balke_41484_fanout_reference), reproduces a comparable R/bd on EURUSD/GBPUSD.
proposed_mechanism: London-session opening-range establishment reflects the first price discovery after the Asia-session low-liquidity book closes and European institutional flow enters; a genuine directional breakout of that range is more likely to be information-driven (continuation) than a Tokyo-session range breakout on the same pair would be, because EURUSD/GBPUSD's natural liquidity center is London, not Tokyo. This is the same economic logic already validated for USDJPY at ITS native session (Tokyo AM, Balke/13213: 0% overnight, 7.2h hold, +0.064R) -- H-V1 pairs the identical mechanism class with EURUSD/GBPUSD's own native session instead of reusing USDJPY's window, directly responding to the README.md section 2c lesson: 'the next fan-outs must pair each mechanism with its own session structure.'

research_question: Does an opening-range breakout/failure mechanism, re-anchored to EURUSD/GBPUSD's own native 07:00-08:00 UTC London cash-session open (instead of the Tokyo window that failed when transplanted onto non-JPY majors), reproduce a session-flat, ~0.5-0.7 trades/bd, >=+0.10R/trade profile comparable to the best measured sleeve (Balke 13213) in the inventory?
